A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learning to Share (LTS). Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original AssistantBench and GAIA experiments, memory-admission comparisons, training-objective ablations, and appendix runtime analyses and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds GAIA experiments on team count, summary length, and orchestrator-based memory admission.

M1.justification: The shared memory bank, controller architecture, training losses, and inference workflow remain unchanged. The orchestrator-controlled variant is an additional experimental comparator; the new summarization details do not establish a change to LTS.

E1.justification: Both versions train on AssistantBench development tasks and evaluate on AssistantBench test tasks and GAIA validation tasks. The added analyses vary internal configurations within GAIA, without adding datasets, domains, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds a full-context orchestrator admission comparator alongside stateless LLM filtering and LTS under Qwen3-32B. Stateless filtering already appeared as LTS-LLM in v1; the existing comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The original splits, metrics, and main evaluation settings are retained. New controlled evaluations vary team count to K=2, 5, and 10 and test 45-50-word summaries against 15-20-word summaries, using the trained controller without retraining.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 substantially expands the analysis beyond the retained loss ablations, memory-utilization studies, and appendix cases. Tables 5-7 newly investigate transfer across team counts, sensitivity to summary length, and whether full-context orchestrator admission can substitute for the learned controller.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables retain point-estimate reporting; the five trajectories per task disclosed for training are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and appendix results are unchanged, but Tables 5-7 add distinct quantitative findings. At K=5, M1-Parallel and LTS score 25.4%/2034s and 31.6%/1234s, respectively. Long summaries yield 29.7%/916s. The Qwen3-32B comparison reports stateless filtering at 26.8%/928s and orchestrator admission at 27.9%/1108s, versus LTS at 30.4%/892s. These are added experimental results, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and controller-training formulation, including Equations 1-10, are retained. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claim: learned selective sharing reduces redundant computation and runtime while preserving or improving task performance. The additional analyses support this existing contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about transfer across team counts and robustness to summary length. It also hypothesizes that trajectory-specific priorities and longer contexts explain the orchestrator comparator's weaker accuracy-runtime tradeoff. Existing limitations concerning per-task memory and absent deletion or revision remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a stateless summarizer using the agent backbone, a 15-20-word summarization target, and approximately 750 tokens per call for a typical 2000-character output. It also describes prompting the full-context orchestrator for admission decisions. Appendix implementation details and access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Works section are unchanged. Section 4.3 adds limited contextualization by explicitly relating the observed performance decline at large team counts to prior M1-Parallel findings.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 becomes 'Ablations and Analysis' with topical subheadings, and the former overhead section becomes a paragraph within it. Other prose receives small edits, and the preprint footer changes to conference-proceedings information; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Three compact tables with captions are added in Section 4.3, causing local reflow of later material. Existing Tables 1-4, Figures 1-3, and appendix figures retain their displays; appendix pages differ only in page numbers.

improvement.justification: Tables 5-7 provide useful checks of previously untested configuration sensitivity and a stronger admission comparator, while the summarization details improve reproducibility. These targeted additions strengthen support for the existing design without replacing earlier evidence. The new results still lack uncertainty estimates, limiting conclusions about small differences.
